verdict.rationale: Clerk documents first-party machine authentication: API keys for programmatic callers and M2M tokens for calls between agents, metered as a platform feature. It also documents gating individual agent tool calls against the caller's permissions and scopes, so a per-agent machine identity with scoped access exists, but how narrowly each agent's credential can be scoped is only implied. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of per-agent least-privilege scoping on API keys/M2M tokens, documented instant revocation of machine credentials (only human session revocation is shown), and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can give each agent its own least-privilege machine identity with narrowly scoped permissions and instant revocation, instead of sharing a human's credentials

citations.quote: An API key authenticates a known programmatic caller — a script, a cron job, a partner's backend — as a Clerk user or org.
Gate individual eve tool calls against the caller's Clerk permissions and scopes
machine authentication (API keys and machine-to-machine tokens) is a metered platform feature across plans
